headline: Warm is only 9.2 percent faster than cold. Caching essentially every routed expert does not materially speed decode, so decode on this artifact is NOT residency-bound or upload-bound. There is a compute/dispatch floor near 6,400 ms per token that residency management cannot remove.

residency.reading: Token 0 loads 13.49 GB -- the fixed backbone plus first routing. Everything after is 95 MB/token and decaying. The working set SATURATES at ~21 GB and never approaches the 32 GiB budget, so the LRU was never exercised.

corrections_to_earlier_claims_by_this_co.claimed: ~1.8 GB of new device residency per token
corrections_to_earlier_claims_by_this_co.cause: Divided 22 GB by 12 tokens without separating the one-time 13.49 GB backbone load from marginal expert growth. The backbone is paid once; treating it as per-token made the slope nearly twenty times too steep.

corrections_to_earlier_claims_by_this_co.claimed: An unbounded cache reaches the whole 92 GB artifact within a few tens of tokens on a 96 GiB host
corrections_to_earlier_claims_by_this_co.actual: Saturates at ~21 GB after 80 tokens with zero evictions
corrections_to_earlier_claims_by_this_co.cause: Followed from the same slope error. Expert reuse is far higher than worst-case routing assumes.
corrections_to_earlier_claims_by_this_co.what_survives: The bound is still correct engineering for long runs, adversarial routing, and hosts shared with other work -- but its empirical urgency was overstated and the catastrophe described does not occur at this scale.

what_this_changes_for_the_campaign: Step 5's honest answer is a floor, not a knob. BASE_TRUE_TPS warm is 0.1547 tok/s and it is compute or dispatch bound. Residency work is finished as an optimisation target -- it earned its place by making the runtime bounded and measurable, not by making it faster, exactly as predicted when the cache was reviewed. The remaining levers are acceleration and kernel work, which raises the value of the spec-decode re-receipt now running.
open_question_next_experiment: The prior verify_hash=false run measured 0.569 tok/s against 0.157 verified, a 3.6x gap -- but that was 12 COLD tokens on General-R0, when every token was verifying hundreds of newly touched tensors. Verification is once per tensor (ensure() short-circuits on a cache hit), so in the warm window it should have largely stopped mattering, yet warm verified sits at 0.1547. Either the residual ~95 MB/token of new tensors still carries the cost, or the floor is elsewhere. A warm verify_hash=false run over the same 80 tokens isolates it. That is the measurement that identifies the dominant decode cost, which gate G2 requires.
not_evidence_of: eviction behaviour under a binding budget -- the LRU was never exercised because the working set never reached the bound
